best_plan.name: p5
best_plan.rationale: Plan p5 gave the same observed quality as p1 (quality 1.0) while lowering execution cost from about $0.00084 to about $0.00050. Although p5 was slower than p1, it still returned five clearly positive reviewIds in a few seconds, so it had the best cost-quality trade-off among the tested plans.

cost_model_explanation: The cost model suggested avoiding several alternative models whose estimated sem_filter costs were much higher, so I focused on variants that changed only the semantic filter model. After execution traces, it was clear the sem_filter operator dominated both cost and latency, while the exact filter, project, and limit were essentially free. GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE was fastest, but GPT_5_NANO achieved the same quality at lower dollar cost, which is why p5 won overall.

plan_codes.p1:
pipeline = PhysicalPipeline(plan_name, "Reviews.csv", load_data("Reviews.csv"))
pipeline.filter(lambda row: isinstance(row["reviewText"], str) and len(row["reviewText"].strip()) > 0)
pipeline.sem_filter(
    "This review text is clearly positive about the movie overall, expressing favorable sentiment without major ambiguity.",
    model=pz.Model.GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE,
    depends_on=["reviewText"]
)
pipeline.project(["reviewId"])
pipeline.limit(5)
pipeline
